To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the unsteady flow through a blade row is influenced by the upstream distortion, and that the distortion wave is attenuated in the downstream flow as it passes the blade row.

the nonlinear large disturbance theory is capable of predicting, for a single blade stage, the onset of a rotating stall cell in the presence of an upstream axial disturbance, the speed of rotation of that cell, and its spatial attenuation.

the distortion wave propagates at the speed of sound in the undisturbed flow, that the distortion wave is attenuated in amplitude as it propagates downstream, and that the onset of rotating stall occurs when the distortion amplitude reaches some critical value.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of an interactive, nonlinear flow analysis which is capable of predicting, in a single blade row, the onset and development of a rotating stall cell in the presence of an upstream axial flow distortion.
the development of a nonlinear, large disturbance analysis of the flow through an axial flow compressor stage.
the prediction of the unsteady fluid dynamic response of an axial flow compressor stage with distorted inflow.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this analysis is a useful tool in the study of the fluid dynamic response of turbomachines to distorted inflow.

the present analysis is capable of predicting, with a high degree of confidence, the unsteady response of an axial flow compressor blade row to an upstream distorted flow field, and that the results obtained are qualitively correct for a single blade.
the theory is capable of predicting, with reasonable accuracy, the onset of a rotating stall pattern and its speed of rotation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the present analysis is able to predict the onset of rotating stall for a single blade and that the speed and attenuation of the distortion is also predicted.
the theory is able to explain the observed behavior of the system and to provide a means for predicting the behavior of other systems.

we are able to predict, in a qualitative manner, the unsteady response of an axial flow compressor to an upstream axial distortion, and that the results of our study are consistent with the limited data available.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distortion is attenuated as it passes through a compressor stage, and the attenuation is greater at lower mass flow rates.
a single row of blades can be used to attenuate the amplitude of the distortion, and the attenuation can be predicted by the theory.
the nonlinear coupling of the blade row and distortion wave analyses is a necessary ingredient in order to obtain reasonable agreement with the experimental data.
